rulings.challenge_claim: The stated ground that no tier-1 marker stands inside web:Jer.6.10-Jer.6.15 is byte-false at three points, and the rival-rejection sentence turns the modern English paragraph division into an affirmative reason for keeping the material together.
rulings.grounds: All three sites re-derive from the bytes. oshb:Jer.6.12 closes נְאֻם יְהוָֽה at byte tier, the chapter's only postpositive divine formula (sweep: 162 verses book-wide; 1 in this chapter, at oshb:Jer.6.12); oshb:Jer.6.15 closes אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה at byte tier; oshb:Jer.6.11 carries the imperative שְׁפֹ֤ךְ at byte tier. The blanket negative-existence wording is therefore byte-false as written, and so is the paired phrase asserting the absence of any tier-1 marker inside the span - the defect is real. Two narrowings. First, the count object behind the second site must be named: the bare amar-YHWH skeleton (sweep: 179 verses) subsumes the koh-amar formula (sweep: 152 verses), so of the 6 chapter verses returned by the blended object only oshb:Jer.6.15 carries a non-koh amar-YHWH close; the byte fact stands, the blended digit does not carry it. Second, the inference that the formula at oshb:Jer.6.12 would argue a sub-seam at 6:12/6:13 overstates its ruled weight: the postpositive divine formula is closure corroboration only and closes a unit only where a fresh tier-1 onset follows, and oshb:Jer.6.13 opens on a causal particle with no onset device, so nothing there argues a cut and the span is not threatened. The tier-4 leg is upheld without narrowing: a modern paragraph division is never-evidence in either direction, and here it is carrying affirmative weight.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace both negative-existence phrases with the byte-true statement - the span carries the imperative at oshb:Jer.6.11, the postpositive divine formula closing oshb:Jer.6.12, and the amar-YHWH close at oshb:Jer.6.15 - and state why none of them cuts (closure corroboration with no fresh tier-1 onset at oshb:Jer.6.13). Delete the clause citing WEB's paragraphing as agreement. strongest_rejected_alternative: drop the paragraphing leg and rest the rival's rejection on the byte-level absence of an onset device at oshb:Jer.6.13. device_notes: add count-only single-witness paseq disclosure for MT 6:11 and MT 6:14 (2 segs; no intra-verse position claim). Test the cure must pass: a formula-and-mark sweep of oshb:Jer.6.10-Jer.6.15 must contradict no remaining negative-existence claim in the row, no field may cite a modern paragraph division as a reason in either direction, and the span's disclosure set must match the inventories at MT keys for parashah, ketiv/qere AND paseq.

rulings.challenge_claim: The seam is sound but its stated ground overstates: oshb:Jer.6.17 does carry a further imperative, embedded in the watchmen's reported call.
rulings.grounds: oshb:Jer.6.17 reads הַקְשִׁ֖יבוּ לְק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָ֑ר at byte tier, rendered “Listen to the sound of the trumpet!” (web:Jer.6.17) - a plural imperative - so the negative-existence wording covering the watchmen verse is byte-false as written. The narrower statement is also the stronger one: the imperative stands inside the watchmen's reported call and is answered in the same verse by וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נַקְשִֽׁיב, reproducing the command-and-refusal shape of oshb:Jer.6.16, which binds 6:17 to 6:16 rather than separating them. The front-seam warrant is untouched: the verse-initial restart at oshb:Jer.6.16 is byte-real and stands in the prophet's report, not inside quoted human speech (sweep: 152 verses carry the koh-amar-YHWH formula; 5 in this chapter, at oshb:Jer.6.6, oshb:Jer.6.9, oshb:Jer.6.16, oshb:Jer.6.21, oshb:Jer.6.22). Low severity is right - the boundary is not disturbed, the supporting ground is. One item the challenge did not reach: the span carries 1 paseq seg at MT 6:16 and the row discloses none.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the no-further-imperative wording with the byte-true reading - the imperative at oshb:Jer.6.17 sits inside reported speech and is answered by the refusal in the same verse, reproducing the command-and-refusal shape of oshb:Jer.6.16 - keeping only the no-koh-amar-restart claim as the negative one. device_notes: add count-only single-witness paseq disclosure for MT 6:16 (1 seg; no intra-verse position claim). Test the cure must pass: an imperative sweep of oshb:Jer.6.16-Jer.6.17 must contradict no remaining negative-existence claim in the row, and the span's disclosure set must match the inventories at MT keys for parashah, ketiv/qere AND paseq.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two items. (a) unit_type judgment_oracle is an undisclosed operative-category deviation because the span pronounces no judgment of its own and matches the closed vocabulary's trial_speech instead. (b) An addressee turn of exactly the class used to cut the front seam falls inside the span at oshb:Jer.6.20, which addresses the offerers and not the witnesses summoned at oshb:Jer.6.18-Jer.6.19, while the backward force of the consequence particle opening oshb:Jer.6.18 goes unweighed at high confidence.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defect claims and they do not both survive. Item (a) is REFUTED on the bytes: oshb:Jer.6.19 carries הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה at byte tier, rendered “Behold, I will bring evil on this people, even the fruit of their thoughts” (web:Jer.6.19) - a first-person divine announcement of coming disaster standing inside the span - so the premise that no judgment content is pronounced anywhere in the span is byte-false, judgment_oracle is a defensible per-bytes typing of a summons-plus-announcement-plus-indictment shape, no closed-vocabulary deviation arises, and no disclosure is owed. Item (b) is UPHELD. oshb:Jer.6.18 summons שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם and, under its own imperative, וּדְעִ֥י עֵדָ֖ה; oshb:Jer.6.19 summons שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ while its body speaks of הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה in the third person; oshb:Jer.6.20 then turns to second-person-plural possessors עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ and וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם, rendered “Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices are not pleasing to me.” (web:Jer.6.20). That suffixed burnt-offerings spelling stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, oshb:Jer.6.20 and oshb:Jer.7.21), and at oshb:Jer.7.21 it is unambiguously the people's own cult addressed under the full divine-title stack - so reading the possessors at 6:20 as the summoned nations and earth is not what the bytes support, and the rival-rejection sentence asserts exactly that. The same addressee-shift class is what cuts this unit's front seam, so the criterion is applied inconsistently and the internal turn is disclosed nowhere. The consequence particle opening oshb:Jer.6.18 (sweep: 55 verses book-wide; 3 in this chapter, at oshb:Jer.6.15, oshb:Jer.6.18, oshb:Jer.6.21) binds the summons back to the refusal reported at oshb:Jer.6.16-Jer.6.17 and, unlike oshb:Jer.6.21, carries no formula overriding it; with neither weight weighed, high confidence is not calibrated. The boundary itself is not decided here.
rulings.remedy: unit_type: leave judgment_oracle unchanged; no deviation disclosure is owed. strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the assertion that Jer.6.20 continues the address to the summoned witnesses and rest the retention of that verse on the shared indictment content instead. device_notes: disclose that the second-person-plural possessors at oshb:Jer.6.20 turn to the people rather than to the nations and the earth summoned at oshb:Jer.6.18-Jer.6.19. boundary_rationale: weigh the backward force of the consequence particle opening oshb:Jer.6.18 against the addressee-shift onset. confidence: lower from high to medium. Any re-cut at 6:19/6:20 is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit adoption, never author work. Test the cure must pass: no field may assert an addressee for oshb:Jer.6.20 that the verse's own suffixes contradict, and any marker class used as a seam criterion must be applied or disclosed wherever the same class recurs inside the span.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unifying ground, a communal first-person-plural voice across the span, is carried by 1 of the span's 2 verses: oshb:Jer.6.25 has no first-person forms, and its two variant notes fall precisely on the addressee number that the unit label and the back seam both rest on.
rulings.grounds: Byte-verified on both legs. oshb:Jer.6.24 carries three first-person-plural forms, שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ, יָדֵ֑ינוּ and הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְנוּ, at byte tier. oshb:Jer.6.25 carries none: it is a negative second-person address, and both of its variant readings stand inline in the source bytes at אַל תצאי תֵּֽצְאוּ֙ and אַל תלכי תֵּלֵ֑כוּ - written forms ending in yod against read forms ending in vav, so the notes vary person-and-number exactly, the count matching the inventory at 2 notes for MT 6:25, one of the twelve doubled-note verses. Under the written form 6:25 stands in the same singular-feminine address paradigm as חִגְרִי and עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ at oshb:Jer.6.26 across the back seam, while oshb:Jer.6.23 already closes כְּאִישׁ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה in that class across the front seam - a byte-true address chain straddling both of this unit's own seams and disclosed at neither. The doubled-note count is disclosed correctly and the variant tokens are correctly kept out of the Hebrew splice; what is missing is the weighing of what those notes vary. The front-seam warrant at 6:23/6:24 is byte-true and stands, and the medium confidence with its not-formula-marked note is honest calibration.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and literature_type_guess: restrict the communal first-person-plural voice to oshb:Jer.6.24 and describe Jer.6.25 by its own bytes as a second-person prohibition. strongest_rejected_alternative: drop the assertion that the communal voice runs across Jer.6.24-Jer.6.25. device_notes: state what the two variant notes at MT 6:25 vary (addressee person-and-number) and disclose that under the written form the verse's address class continues into oshb:Jer.6.26 across the back seam and matches the class already closing oshb:Jer.6.23 across the front seam. Test the cure must pass: every voice or addressee label must hold for every verse of the span it is asserted of, checked verse by verse against the pointed bytes, and any ketiv/qere note bearing on a label or a seam must be weighed rather than merely counted.

rulings.challenge_claim: The voice contrast this cut rests on is byte-contested on both sides of its own front seam: oshb:Jer.6.26 itself closes with a first-person-plural suffix, and oshb:Jer.6.25 has no first-person forms.
rulings.grounds: Both byte facts confirm. oshb:Jer.6.26 closes עָלֵֽינוּ at byte tier, rendered “for the destroyer will suddenly come on us” (web:Jer.6.26) - and the row quotes that same clause as its own content while declaring the verse distinct from the communal first-person-plural voice, so a byte-true device straddles the front seam undisclosed, which under cross-seam cohesion argues continuity against the unit. oshb:Jer.6.25 in turn carries no first-person form at all, so the material the verse is contrasted with does not carry the contrasted voice where the contrast is drawn. Both legs are real. The framing is what needs correcting: the cut does not rest on the voice contrast. Its stated onset warrant is the verse-initial vocative-plus-imperative בַּת עַמִּ֤י חִגְרִי שָׂק֙ at byte tier, and the rival-rejection sentence rests on the marker class, comparing כַּבְּסִ֨י מֵרָעָ֤ה לִבֵּךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם at oshb:Jer.4.14 and הָעִ֣זוּ בְּנֵ֣י בִניָמִ֗ן at oshb:Jer.6.1 - all three byte-confirmed as imperative-plus-vocative address to a named or personified addressee. The seam warrant therefore survives; what fails is the discriminating clause and the undisclosed continuity, and the severity attaches to the disclosure defect, not to the boundary.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete or re-cut the clause declaring the verse distinct from the communal first-person-plural voice of Jer.6.24-Jer.6.25, and disclose instead that the verse's own closing first-person-plural suffix at oshb:Jer.6.26 continues the communal voice of oshb:Jer.6.24 across the front seam while the vocative-plus-imperative onset carries the cut. Correct any remaining characterisation of Jer.6.24-Jer.6.25 as jointly communal. confidence: high may stand only if the re-cut rationale rests solely on the onset marker class; otherwise lower to medium. Test the cure must pass: no field may contrast the span against a voice the span's own bytes carry, and every byte-true device straddling a seam must be disclosed as continuity argued against.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unpointed place-name spelling is quoted at skeleton grade with no tier label where the row's other Hebrew runs carry one, and the three-forms count beside it is hung on the preposition-prefixed token rather than on the name spelling it actually counts.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed on the bytes. The row carries four Hebrew runs; three are labelled byte tier and the fourth - the bare consonantal spelling quoted for the place-name - is unlabelled and, being unpointed, reaches only skeleton grade; it is also re-keyed rather than spliced, which is exactly the copy-degradation hazard the engagement rule forbids for this substrate. The count object is mis-hung as claimed: what is quoted as one of three forms is the preposition-prefixed token, while the three forms belong to the name spelling itself - byte-checkable inside this row's own chapter, where oshb:Jer.7.12 reads בְּשִׁיל֔וֹ and oshb:Jer.7.14 reads לְשִׁלֽוֹ, two different name spellings under two different prefixes. The sentence names neither the swept object nor its unit and carries no digit, which per-site count discipline requires before any digit for this name. The boundary is not contested and is byte-sound: the header at oshb:Jer.7.1 is a true member of the prose-sermon superscription shape (sweep: 11 verses), the stack at oshb:Jer.7.3 a true member of the full divine-title object (sweep: 32 verses) spoken in the divine mouth through the prophet, and the end warrant at oshb:Jer.7.16 is a marked second-person-singular pronoun with prohibition. Low severity is right. One item the challenge did not reach: the parashah and ketiv/qere accounting for this span is complete, but the span carries 2 paseq segs at MT 7:9 and MT 7:14 and the row discloses none.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the re-keyed unpointed spelling with a programmatic splice of the pointed form from source at oshb:Jer.7.12 with its tier named, or keep a consonantal form and label it skeleton tier explicitly. Re-cut the count sentence so it names the swept object (the place-name spelling, read per attested site) and its unit and carries a digit in the sanctioned sweep form, distinguishing the name spelling from the preposition-prefixed token. device_notes: add count-only single-witness paseq disclosure for MT 7:9 and MT 7:14 (2 segs; no intra-verse position claim). Test the cure must pass: every Hebrew run in the row re-collates against its cited reference with the matched tier named, every count claim names its swept object and unit before its digit, and the span's disclosure set matches the inventories at MT keys for parashah, ketiv/qere AND paseq.

rulings.challenge_claim: The continuity warrant for keeping the consequence clause inside the unit is byte-false on its referent half: the place-noun it names does not occur anywhere in the prohibition it is said to continue, and the book's one adonai-YHWH title stack at that verse is dismissed as emphasis without being weighed.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed on the bytes. The stated warrant is that the closing verse keeps the same speaker and the same referent, this place, as the prohibition. The speaker half is byte-true; the referent half is not. The noun stands in 6 verses of this chapter (sweep: 6 verses, oshb:Jer.7.3, oshb:Jer.7.6, oshb:Jer.7.7, oshb:Jer.7.14, oshb:Jer.7.20, oshb:Jer.7.32) and none of them falls inside oshb:Jer.7.16-Jer.7.19. The prohibition's own referent is הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה at oshb:Jer.7.16, byte tier, while הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה enters at oshb:Jer.7.20 and nowhere earlier in the span (sweep: 15 verses book-wide carry the full demonstrative phrase; 1 in this chapter, at oshb:Jer.7.20). Corrected, the noun is a catchword reaching backward across this unit's own front seam to וְלַ֨מָּק֔וֹם at oshb:Jer.7.14, which argues cohesion with the preceding material and is disclosed nowhere. One narrowing on the second leg: the title at oshb:Jer.7.20 is indeed the book's only koh-amar adonai-YHWH stack (sweep: 1 verse), but under the ruled granularity a speech-formula onset cuts only with a change of frame owner and the mouth does not change here, so treating the formula as non-seam is the policy-correct disposition; the defect there is the missing disclosure of a uniquely attested title site, not the retention of the verse. The cut itself can stand on the consequence connective the row does splice and on its correct parashah disclosures.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the claim that the closing verse keeps the same referent as the prohibition and replace it with the byte-true referents - this people at oshb:Jer.7.16 against this place at oshb:Jer.7.20 - resting retention on the consequence connective and the unchanged divine speaker. device_notes: disclose that the place-noun catchword reaches back across the front seam to oshb:Jer.7.14 and is argued against rather than ignored, and disclose that oshb:Jer.7.20 is the book's single koh-amar adonai-YHWH stack site with a digit-bearing sweep count naming the object and unit; add count-only single-witness paseq disclosure for MT 7:16 and MT 7:20 (2 segs; no intra-verse position claim). Test the cure must pass: any referent or catchword continuity asserted between two verses of a span must be present in both, verified by a chapter-internal sweep naming the noun; every byte-true device straddling a seam must be disclosed; and the span's disclosure set must match the inventories at MT keys for parashah, ketiv/qere AND paseq.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row names the feminine-singular addressee at its onset as personified Zion, a name absent from the chapter's bytes; and the judgment formula at oshb:Jer.7.32 is called recurring with a tier label but no count.
rulings.grounds: Both confirmed. The form claim itself is byte-true: גָּזִּ֤י נִזְרֵךְ֙ וְֽהַשְׁלִ֔יכִי וּשְׂאִ֥י at oshb:Jer.7.29, byte tier, carries three feminine-singular imperatives and a feminine-singular suffix, so the address change at the onset is real. The named referent is not: the place-name stands in 16 verses book-wide and 0 in this chapter (sweep: 16 verses; nearest site oshb:Jer.8.19), the bytes leave the addressee unnamed, and the feminine figure actually attested in the neighbourhood is the daughter-of-my-people figure (sweep: 9 verses, including oshb:Jer.6.26 and oshb:Jer.8.19). Naming a referent the bytes withhold is a byte-checkable claim failing the same discipline as an unswept digit, and it is the identification the onset warrant leans on. The second item is real too: the formula at oshb:Jer.7.32 is called recurring with a tier label and no digit (sweep: 15 verses book-wide). Everything else in the row verifies - the temporal resumption at oshb:Jer.8.1 is byte-true and correctly kept out of the dated-header inventory, belonging to a seven-verse temporal-resumption object (sweep: 7 verses); the end warrant at oshb:Jer.8.4 is a commission plus formula in the divine mouth; and the span's parashah and ketiv/qere disclosures match the inventories at MT keys. Low severity is right. One item the challenge did not reach: the span carries 3 paseq segs at MT 7:34, MT 8:1 and MT 8:2 and the row discloses none.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the named referent with the byte-attested description - an unnamed feminine-singular addressee - or, if an identification is retained, mark it as inference and cite the sweep showing the name is absent from the chapter. Attach a digit-bearing sweep count in the sanctioned form to the recurrence claim for the formula at oshb:Jer.7.32, naming the swept object and its unit. device_notes: add count-only single-witness paseq disclosure for MT 7:34, MT 8:1 and MT 8:2 (3 segs; no intra-verse position claim). Test the cure must pass: every named referent in the row is attested in the span's own bytes or explicitly flagged as inference; every recurrence claim carries its swept object, unit and digit; and the span's disclosure set matches the inventories at MT keys for parashah, ketiv/qere AND paseq.

supported_sample.claim_checked: The onset at oshb:Jer.6.27 is a second-person-masculine-singular address to the prophet, a fresh addressee for this closing unit.
supported_sample.notes: Re-derived from source bytes: oshb:Jer.6.27 reads בָּח֛וֹן נְתַתִּ֥יךָ בְעַמִּ֖י מִבְצָ֑ר at byte tier, whose verb carries the second-person-masculine-singular object suffix, and the following וְתֵדַ֕ע and וּבָחַנְתָּ֖ are second-person-masculine-singular verbs - so the form-class label rests on the pointed bytes and not on either witness's rendering. The change is visible on both sides of the seam: the verse immediately before the onset addresses a feminine singular, חִגְרִי and וְהִתְפַּלְּשִׁ֣י at oshb:Jer.6.26, byte tier. The span's disclosure set also checks against the inventories at MT keys: 1 variant note at MT 6:29, correctly kept out of the Hebrew splice, and the petuchah closing MT 6:30, both disclosed under their correct and distinct types; the span carries 0 paseq segs and 0 further marks, so nothing further is owed - the only span among the adjudicated set with a complete disclosure account.
